Photograph: Owen Humphreys/PA North Yorkshire ‘These were brave officers’: tributes paid to police among seven killed in A66 crash Redcar MP says Teesside community is ‘reeling’ as PM offers condolences and asks public to avoid speculation Mark Brown North of England correspondent Sun 23 Aug 2026 06.43 EDT First published on Sun 23 Aug 2026 04.30 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google Tributes are being paid to two police officers who died on Teesside when a car travelling the wrong way along the A66 crashed head-on into their vehicle, also killing five young men. PC Matthew Blades, 37, and PC Tom Clough, 38, were killed when the marked armed response vehicle they were in was struck by a Volkswagen Passat in the early hours of Saturday morning. On Sunday, Anna Turley, the Home Office minister and local Redcar MP, said it was “devastating” to think about the grief of the families of everyone who lost their lives on Saturday morning. The whole community was “reeling”, she said. “All of us in the community here are sending our heartfelt thoughts and sympathies to the families and loved ones of those who lost their lives so tragically,” she told BBC Breakfast. Turley said it was important to avoid speculation about what might have happened and allow families the privacy to grieve. “I do want to place on record my tribute to PC Blades and PC Clough. The bravery that we see from our police officers every day, every night is incredible. No one should not come home to their families at the end of their shift.” She also said it was important to thank the emergency services who attended at the scene during “a really horrific incident”. Security camera footage from local houses appeared to show the police pursuit moments before the fatal crash on the A66. Security camera footage appears to show police pursuit minutes before fatal A66 crash Andy Burnham said he was “devastated” to hear two police officers had lost their lives on duty, as well as five members of the public. The prime minister said: “My thoughts are with the families and loved ones of everyone involved, and with everyone at Cleveland police. Thank you to the emergency services responding in incredibly difficult circumstances. I would urge people to avoid speculation at this time.” The Cleveland police chief constable, Victoria Fuller, said she and her deputy had on Saturday visited the families of the two officers to offer condolences and support. “This is an incredibly sad day for Cleveland,” she said. “This loss is being felt across our communities, by our police family and by our partner agencies. These were brave officers, protecting our communities and serving our residents, who didn’t return home to their families at the end of their shift.” View image in fullscreen Cleveland police chief constable, Victoria Fuller, said it was an ‘incredibly sad day’. Photograph: Owen Humphreys/PA Lauren Somerville, the chair of Cleveland police federation, said the grief among officers was “all-consuming, overwhelming”. She said: “Words cannot describe the pain the Cleveland police family are feeling.” The Tees Valley mayor, Ben Houchen, said in a statement on Facebook : “A horrible and tragic incident in South Bank this morning and my thoughts are with those affected, their families and the emergency services who attended the scene. “Our police officers are heroes who put everything on the line to protect us, and I know all of Teesside will want to pay tribute to the officers and other emergency service workers involved for the bravery they have shown in responding to this incident.” The five young men in the VW Passat have not been named by authorities, although they have been named on social media. The Independent Office for Police Conduct has opened an investigation into the circumstances leading to the crash at 3.39am in South Bank after a mandatory referral from Cleveland police. Police vehicles had been pursuing the car before it joined the A66 although it is understood the pursuit had ended before the fatal crash. Ring doorbell footage published by several websites minutes before the crash shows a car being driven at speed down a residential road and being followed by police cars. Ellie Westerman, who lives locally, told the Sun: “The noise woke me and I shot out of bed. You could feel the vibration in the house as the car went past and the police vehicles followed with their lights and sirens going. It was frightening that cars were being driven at that speed through a residential area.” Explore more on these topics North Yorkshire Middlesbrough Police news Share Reuse this content More on this story More on this story ‘Saltburn are the Argentina of local cricket’: victims and neighbours on the ‘Clicky Ponting’ scandal Here be dragons: does moving power to the north work? https://www.euronews.com/2026/11/08/ross.text: The hacker groups Kiberpartizany BY and Silent Crow claim to have carried out a large-scale breach of Russia's Federal State Statistics Service (Rosstat).According to the hackers, they managed to steal about 23 terabytes of data, including internal documents, demographic and economic statistics, as well as information on Russian losses in the war against Ukraine.The data obtained enabled the groups to make their own calculations of the number of people killed since the start of Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022.According to Kiberpartizany BY, as of 27 August 2026 at least 393,881 Russian citizens have been killed in the war. Silent Crow gives an even higher figure of 450,100 dead.This significant difference in estimates is due to the use of different methods of counting losses.Kiberpartizany BY counted deaths in which military action or its consequences were listed as the cause.Silent Crow, by contrast, not only included those killed in combat, but also added several other categories of deaths: non-combat losses among military personnel, deaths marked as terrorist acts, and deaths of people registered in Russia but who died in occupied territories or in Ukraine where the exact cause of death was not established.Why these figures are particularly importantRussia has not released official statistics on combat losses since September 2022.In addition, from 2024 Rosstat stopped publishing annual data on causes of death, which has made an independent assessment of the demographic impact of the war much more difficult.Against this backdrop, access to the agency's internal statistical materials may make it possible to assess the scale of human losses more accurately.For comparison, as of 8 November the joint database of BBC News Russian Service and Mediazona, which collects a list of dead Russian servicemen identified by name, contained around 286,000 names. However, this list is known to be incomplete, especially for the most recent months of the war.In a joint study by Meduza and Mediazona, based on analysis of inheritance registry data, the number of fallen Russian servicemen by the end of 2025 was estimated at roughly 350,000.In this way, the hackers' estimates are in line with figures from previously published independent studies, although this does not yet prove the accuracy of each individual number.Verifying the authenticity of the dataMeduza and Mediazona have said they obtained access to the data published by the hackers and have begun checking it.The journalists aim to establish not only whether the materials are authentic, but also how complete the information is they contain. In particular, they need to rule out the possibility of deliberate data falsification.Moreover, causes of death given in medical documents do not always reflect the actual circumstances of a person's death.It should also be noted that Rosstat's internal databases do not contain up-to-date information on people listed as missing. Such individuals may be declared dead only after a long period of time.Therefore even data from the state statistics agency cannot automatically provide a definitive figure for Russian military losses.If the authenticity and completeness of the leak are confirmed, the materials obtained could become one of the largest sources of information on the demographic consequences of the war for Russia.
